title: How this guide plays
brief: You have an hour with a group, or twenty minutes alone. Learn the loop each level follows, where your progress lives and which study path fits your time and your gaps.

blocks.title: Every problem level follows the same eight steps

steps.title: Brief
steps.md: A problem with its constraints left open on purpose.

steps.title: Options board
steps.md: Every sensible option, with pros, cons, best-when and avoid-when.

steps.title: Flip the dials
steps.md: Change scale, permissions, latency, risk or cost and watch the ranking and the reasons move.

steps.title: Failure modes
steps.md: Symptom, root cause and fix for what usually goes wrong.

steps.title: Quiz
steps.md: Single choice, multi select, ordering, matching, numeric and bug-spotting items.

steps.title: Defend it
steps.md: Write an interview-style answer, reveal the model answer, score yourself with the rubric.

steps.title: Flashcards
steps.md: Spaced-repetition cards that build up across worlds.

steps.title: References
steps.md: Dated links to specs, vendor docs, papers and courses.

items: Progress lives in this browser's local storage on this computer. It is never sent anywhere, and the guide works with no network.
Clearing site data or switching browsers removes your progress. Export first from the footer or the Progress page.
To move to another browser or computer, export a file and import it there. Importing can merge with existing progress or replace it.
If the browser blocks local storage, a banner says so and the guide keeps progress in memory until you export.

head: Keys
What they do
rows: Close search, a dialog or the navigation drawer
Switch between light and dark theme
Open the help page at the shortcuts
Quiz: choose an option, then check the answer
Flashcards: flip the card, then grade it

blocks.md: Seven interactive labs sit inside the worlds where the idea matters. World 2 holds `kv-cache`, `prompt-cache` and `latency-budget`. World 4 holds `chunk-visualizer`, world 5 holds `rrf-playground`, world 7 holds `acl-simulator` and world 10 holds `context-budget`. Each lab ends with three guided experiments.

head: Board
Use it to
rows: Read each option's pros, cons, best-when and avoid-when
Flip constraints and see the ranking and the reasons update
Separate what you know from what you must ask
Match a symptom to a cause and a fix
Check the numbers behind a decision
Go deeper without cluttering the main path

blocks.caption: Run one world as a workshop
head: Step
What the facilitator does
Time
rows: Pick one world per session. Most worlds take 60 to 90 minutes. Ask everyone to open the guide from the same zip so the content matches.
It shows quiz answers and model answers with an Answer key badge. Keep it off on the learners' screens.
Run each level in four moves
Read the brief aloud. Let pairs flip the dials and argue. Take the quiz. Run the defend task with its timebox, then compare against the rubric.
Ask what would change the choice. Good answers name a dial and a threshold.
Ask each learner to export progress and share the file. The dashboard shows weak topics to coach next.

blocks.title: Three study paths
blocks.intro: Pick by how much time you have and how much you already know.

options.name: Sequential tour
options.summary: Work through w00 to w19 in order.
pros: Every dial is introduced before it is used
cons: Slow if you already know a region
options.bestWhen: You are new to GenAI engineering and have several weeks.

options.name: Gap-driven
options.summary: Use the dashboard to find weak topics and revisit those levels.
pros: Spends time where you are weakest
options.bestWhen: You have finished a first pass and want to close gaps.
options.avoidWhen: You have no quiz history yet.

options.name: Interview sprint
options.summary: Do the boss levels and defend tasks first, then read the levels behind each miss.
pros: Practises speaking structure under a timebox
cons: Boss levels assume the earlier worlds
options.bestWhen: You know the basics and need fluency in days.
options.avoidWhen: You cannot yet name the dials of a system.

blocks.title: Say it out loud
blocks.md: The defend task rewards structure, and you build structure by speaking it. Answer aloud against the timebox before you reveal the model answer, then score yourself with the rubric.

quiz.q: Select every true statement about your progress in this guide.
options: It is saved in browser local storage on this computer
Switching to another browser keeps it automatically
Importing a file can merge with or replace existing progress
Exported files are uploaded to a server for backup
If local storage is blocked, a banner appears and progress stays in memory until you export
quiz.explain: Progress is local to the browser, so switching browsers loses it unless you export and import. Nothing is ever uploaded, and a blocked local storage falls back to memory with a banner.

quiz.q: A facilitator projects the guide on a screen the whole group can see. Which setting should be off, and why?
options: Dark theme, because it hides the dials from people far from the screen
The sidebar, because it distracts the group from the quiz questions
Facilitator mode, because it shows the answers
Local storage, because it records every answer the group gives
quiz.explain: Facilitator mode shows answers with an Answer key badge, so it spoils the quiz and the defend task on a shared screen. Theme and sidebar do not affect learning, and local storage keeps data private to the browser.

takeaways: Every problem level runs the same loop: brief, options, dials, failures, quiz, defend, cards, references
Progress is local to the browser, so export before you clear data or switch machines
Facilitator mode reveals answers, so keep it off on learners' screens
Choose the study path by time and gaps, and always practise the defend task aloud
